I keep checking the weather app, and the second I hear thunder or see lightning, my chest tightens, my heart races, I feel like I’m about to… I don’t know, lose control or something. Even strong wind at night freaks me out. I’ll turn off my music and just sit there listening, completely on edge, like something bad is about to happen outside.

Food has gotten weird for me too. Sometimes I hesitate before eating certain things—like meat, bread, or anything stringy or with weird textures—because I get this image in my head of choking or throwing up. If I see lightning through the window or hear thunder start to rumble, my heart just slams in my chest, my hands shake, I start sweating, and I feel like I can’t breathe properly. Sometimes I crawl into the bathroom and sit on the floor with my headphones on, because even seeing the sky go dark makes me feel like something terrible is about to happen. I avoid going out if the weather app says there’s any chance of storms, even if I’m already behind on deadlines.

I’ve also developed this intense fear of certain foods, especially anything with bones or stringy textures—like chicken, fish, or even some vegetables. I’m terrified I’ll choke or throw up. It’s not about calories or my weight; I actually worry I’m too thin from skipping meals. I’ll just eat soft, “safe” foods instead, even if I’m starving, because the idea of choking makes me panic the same way storms do.

It’s been on my mind more the last few months. I’ve always been a bit squeamish, but lately anything to do with blood or needles really sets me off. If I even see a scene in a movie with someone getting an injection, I start to feel lightheaded and my hands get clammy. When I had to get some routine blood work recently, I nearly walked out of the clinic. I only went through with it because my sister came with me and sat right beside me. I kept my eyes shut, squeezed the little stuffed owl I bring in my bag, and tried to focus on my breathing.  

Something similar happens with certain foods. I get nervous about swallowing wrong or throwing up, especially if it’s something tough or stringy, like meat. I find myself cutting things into very tiny pieces or just pushing them around on my plate. It’s not really about how I look, at least not that I’m aware of; it’s more this nagging worry that something bad might happen if I’m not careful.

I put off blood tests for as long as I can, and when I absolutely have to go, I only manage it if a friend comes with me and sits right next to me. I grip her hand the whole time and stare at the floor; otherwise I feel like I’ll faint.

There’s also this fear about certain foods. I’m not avoiding them to lose weight or anything—I’m not focused on my body size—but I’m scared I’ll choke or throw up. I’ll skip meals and say I’m “not hungry” at work, or I’ll eat just a few crackers and an apple and tell myself I’ve eaten enough for the day. I count calories in my head constantly and I avoid anything I think could make me gain even a little weight.  

I’ve also started getting scared around certain foods because I feel like if I eat them I’ll lose control and it’ll show on the scale. I worry about choking or throwing up in public, but underneath that it’s really about not wanting my body to change or look bigger.  

On top of that, I’ve always had this awful reaction to blood and needles. If I even see a blood drive poster in the hallway, I get lightheaded. For blood tests, I’ll only go if a friend comes and sits with me; I have to grip their hand and look away or I feel like I might pass out.
